card.summary: Text→video on the original HunyuanVideo 13B (Q8_0 GGUF, 24 GB). Guidance-distilled (embedded FluxGuidance ~6, no negative). The text→video counterpart to the i2v GGUF editor.
card.pick_when: You want a HunyuanVideo text→video clip on a 24 GB card.

prompt.guidance: Describe the motion/scene; the prompt directs the motion.
prompt.example: a fox running through a snowy forest at dawn, tracking shot, soft morning light, cinematic
prompt.overview: Write one flowing natural-language description (subject + action + scene + optional camera/lighting/atmosphere/style), not comma-separated tags.
prompt.instructions: The original HunyuanVideo 13B (LLaVA-Llama3 + CLIP-L encoders) was trained on structured, rewritten natural-language captions, so prompt in descriptive English sentences rather than tags. The t2v model benefits from a richer single paragraph; the official PromptRewrite tool's Normal mode clarifies intent while Master mode adds composition/lighting/camera-movement detail for higher visual quality. The standard t2v checkpoint is CFG/guidance-distilled, so a true negative prompt has little effect - steer via the positive prompt. Decompose a complex action into a short ordered sequence of states.
do: Write natural-language sentences/paragraphs, not tag lists or weight syntax
Order elements as Subject -> Action -> Scene/Background -> Camera, plus optional lighting/style
Use explicit camera/motion language ('the camera slowly pushes in', 'tracking shot', 'static shot')
Decompose a complex action into an ordered sequence ('they stand apart, then move closer, then embrace')
Add lighting, atmosphere, and style cues for higher visual quality
Steer with the distilled guidance scale rather than a negative prompt
dont: Don't use SD-style tag lists or weight syntax like (word:1.2)
Don't rely on a negative prompt; the distilled t2v checkpoint largely ignores it
Don't apply HunyuanVideo 1.5's handbook formulas to the original 13B
Don't cram multiple unrelated actions or rapid scene changes into one prompt
Don't omit the subject/scene (t2v invents everything from text)
examples: A lone astronaut walks across a vast orange desert under a pale alien sky, kicking up fine dust with each step; the camera slowly tracks alongside in a low-angle shot, warm late-afternoon sunlight casting long shadows, cinematic, photorealistic.
prompt.negative_guidance: The original 13B t2v release is CFG/guidance-distilled (embedded guidance ~6.0), so a conventional negative prompt is largely ineffective - steer entirely via the positive prompt.
